prompt.en: Why are leaves not black? Write your own view first.

viewpoints.en: Chlorophyll's ancestors evolved in water, under early bacteria that absorbed green and left red and blue to reach deeper. A pigment that caught the leftovers won, and its descendants kept it. Leaves are green because of who lived above them long ago.

Full sun delivers more light than a leaf can use; the towers from V.9 L03 jam if photons come too fast, and excess lifts make damaging molecules. Throwing back the brightest colour may protect the machinery. Green is a sunshade.

Catching red and blue, at the edges of the sun's spectrum, gives a steadier supply as clouds and canopy shift, because the middle varies most. A steady input beats a big one for a machine that cannot store lifted electrons.
None of these is proven, and more than one could be true at once. A living thing's design is history plus physics, and history does not always pick the best physics.

image.alt: A leaf held up to sunlight passing through a prism, three candidate reasons floating around it for why it reflects green rather than absorbing every colour.
